subject: Retention windows & export granularity for tenant audit traces — Q&A
messages:
From: security@finvero.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Clarify tenant audit trace retention/export granularity

Hi Vanessa,

We're running through our evidence checklist ahead of the regulator review next quarter. Two quick items we need cleared up for tenant audit traces:

1) Retention windows: can you confirm the minimum and maximum retention windows you support for access/audit traces at the tenant level (we saw references to 90/365/999-day profiles but need concrete options and any constraints for EU tenants)?

2) Export granularity: when we request an export, are snapshots produced only at daily boundaries, or can we request a time-range sliced export (e.g., 2026-03-11T16:00 -> 2026-03-13T03:00) with per-event timestamps preserved? Also curious about whether exported manifests include checksums and sequence ids to verify completeness.

Please advise and let us know any lead time required for larger exports (multi-month). Attaching our checklist (no PII).

Thanks,
--
Lucas M.
Head of Security, FinVero
security@finvero.com

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: security@finvero.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-14T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify tenant audit trace retention/export granularity

Hi Lucas — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers first, then a couple of operational notes and asks so we can scope an export if you want it processed.

Retention windows (EU tenants):
- Minimum configurable: 30 days (short retention profile).
- Typical preset tiers: 90 days, 365 days.
- Long-term: up to 1095 days (3 years) for customers on enterprise retention add-on (requires contract amendment).
- Constraints: for EU-resident tenants we persist event indices in-region; deletion is triggered by scheduled TTL job that runs in the tenant's primary region. Immediate deletion on demand is available only under a supported erase playbook and may take up to 72 hours for queued indices to be purged across replicas.

Export granularity and formats:
- Time-range exports: yes — we support arbitrary start/end timestamps (ISO8601) for slice exports. Exports are built from stored event fragments and preserve per-event timestamps and actor metadata.
- Snapshot cadence: daily snapshotting is used for long-term archival bundles, but ad-hoc range exports are rendered on demand from the event store, not necessarily tied to a daily snapshot.
- Manifest: exports include a manifest.csv (schema attached) with per-file checksums (SHA256), sequence ranges, and counts. We also produce a sample index (jsonl) that maps event ids -> file offsets for large exports to make integrity checks faster.

Performance & lead time:
- Small slices (<24h or <10M events): usually available within a few hours.
- Large slices (weeks/months): we recommend a 3–5 business day lead time for bulk exports >100M events so we can allocate export workers and generate signed URLs.

Operational asks from our side to scope work:
- Confirm tenant ID + preferred time window (ISO timezone).
- Any legal-hold flags currently active? If yes, we will freeze deletion but export behavior is unchanged.
- Delivery preference: S3 signed URLs (EU region) or encrypted transfer via Secure FTP?

Attaching: audit_manifest_schema_v1.csv and sample_snapshot_index.jsonl (example lines). I flagged Marissa for bandwidth planning and Soojin for deletion/erase playbook details.

Best,
--
Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-16T08:24:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify tenant audit trace retention/export granularity

Hi Lucas — following up with concrete operational details from the Ops team: 

- Export delivery: for EU tenants we push signed S3 URLs in eu-central-1 by default. If you require another cloud region or a cloud storage endpoint (customer-owned bucket), please provide the bucket ARN + write role.
- File structure: exports are chunked in 100MB gzipped files (events.jsonl.gz), a manifest.csv with file name, start_ts, end_ts, sha256, event_count, and an index.jsonl that lists first_event_id,last_event_id for each chunk.
- Integrity: we provide a top-level export checksum (SHA256 over concatenated per-file checksums) and a line-count sanity check. For particularly critical audits we can provide a signed attest (PGP) for the manifest.
- Deletion interplay: if an erase is requested while an export is in progress, the export completes using the data snapshot taken at export start; deletion will proceed after export finalization.
- Cost/quotas: large exports will be billed as egress + export processing hours; we'll provide an estimate once you confirm scope.

Next steps from our side: please reply with the tenant_id and the exact ISO start/end range you want. If you need proof-of-erase after export, include that request so we can coordinate the erase playbook (note: proof-of-erase includes tombstone records and a verification report, delivery within 5 business days).

Thanks,
--
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
